incidents.title: Connection pool exhaustion causing payment timeouts
symptoms: p95 latency on payments-service jumped from ~150ms to >4000ms
Error rate rose from 0.3% to 22%
Logs flooded with ConnectionPoolTimeoutException: Timeout waiting for connection from pool
incidents.root_cause: A retry-storm from the checkout-service during a downstream card-processor slowdown held DB connections open longer than expected, exhausting the payments-service connection pool (max=100).
incidents.resolution: Restarted the payments-service pods to release stuck connections, then shipped a fix that added a connection checkout timeout and capped retry attempts. Pool size was later increased from 100 to 150 as a buffer.
incidents.matches_query: Sample query 2 & 3 in requirements.md ('has this happened before' / connection-pool exhaustion runbook)

incidents.title: Latency regression after deploy v2.1.0
symptoms: p95 latency on checkout-service jumped ~5x within 10 minutes of deploying v2.1.0
Error rate rose from 0.4% to 9%
No infrastructure alerts fired; correlated tightly with deploy timestamp
incidents.root_cause: v2.1.0 introduced a synchronous call to a new fraud-scoring endpoint on the request hot path, which added ~600ms of blocking latency per checkout request.
incidents.resolution: On-call engineer rolled back to v2.0.9 via the standard human-approved rollback process. Latency and error rate returned to baseline within 5 minutes of rollback completing.
incidents.matches_query: Sample query 1 & 4 in requirements.md (latency spike triage / rollback refusal)

incidents.title: Cache stampede after cache-node failover
symptoms: auth-service p95 latency doubled from ~80ms to ~170ms
Redis CPU utilization spiked to 95%+
Elevated 5xx rate on login endpoint (~4%)
incidents.root_cause: A cache node failover caused a large fraction of session-lookup keys to expire simultaneously, triggering a thundering-herd of cache-miss lookups against the primary DB.
incidents.resolution: Enabled request coalescing (single-flight) for session lookups and staggered cache TTLs to avoid synchronized expiry.

incidents.title: Card-processor authorization failures due to expired TLS certificate
symptoms: 100% of charge-authorization requests failing immediately (TLS handshake failure, not a timeout)
Error rate at 100% for the full duration
No processor-side status page incident reported
incidents.root_cause: The mTLS client certificate used to authenticate with the card-processor API expired silently -- no automated renewal or expiry alerting existed.
incidents.resolution: On-call engineer manually rotated in a pre-generated backup certificate from the secrets vault, restoring processor connectivity within minutes.

incidents.title: Checkout failures due to inventory-service timeout during flash-sale traffic
symptoms: ~15% of checkout requests failing with inventory-check timeouts
inventory-service p99 latency exceeding checkout-service's 3s timeout
Correlated with a promotional flash-sale traffic spike
incidents.root_cause: inventory-service had no autoscaling policy and was not provisioned for the promotional traffic spike; its DB query latency degraded under load, pushing p99 past checkout-service's inventory-check timeout.
incidents.resolution: On-call manually scaled inventory-service from 6 to 20 pods; latency recovered within ~10 minutes.

incidents.title: auth-service pod crash loop due to memory leak in session-cache client
symptoms: Login error rate rose to ~6% as pods cycled through OOM kills
p95 login latency rose from ~80ms to ~300ms during pod churn
Pod restart count alert firing repeatedly
incidents.root_cause: A recently upgraded session-cache client library had a connection-object leak that accumulated memory on every cache access, exhausting each pod's memory limit after ~2 hours of runtime.
incidents.resolution: On-call rolled back the session-cache client library to the previous version and restarted affected pods; memory usage stabilized.
